title: What Is Mercury Capsule? — Definition
body:
The first space age: Goddard's rockets, the V-2, Sputnik and the Space Race, Mercury/Gemini/Apollo, early satellites (Telstar, weather, spy), and the ground stations, tracking networks, and computers that reached the Moon with less computing than a pocket calculator.

In the context of this database, the Mercury Capsule is presented as one space history record among the early space history family. 1959's 1-man: the 1959 — the 1963's.

title: Origins and History of Mercury Capsule
body:
The Mercury Capsule belongs to the 1959–1963 era and traces to McDonnell.

Goddard launched the first liquid-fuel rocket (1926); the German V-2 (1944) weaponized it. Captured V-2s seeded US and Soviet programs; Sputnik (1957) shocked America into NASA (1958). Gagarin (1961) and Glenn (1962) put humans up; Telstar (1962) relayed TV across the Atlantic. Gemini (1965–66) learned rendezvous and spacewalking; Apollo (1968–72) landed twelve men on the Moon with the AGC's 72K of rope memory. The era's computers were heroic minimalism; its tracking network (Minitrack, MSFN) spanned the globe.

Within that longer story, Mercury Capsule: The 1959; the 6 manned. The Mercury is the 1-man's capsule.

title: How Mercury Capsule Works
body:
Rockets throw mass backward to go forward (Tsiolkovsky, 1903): staging drops dead weight, and the rocket equation sets the brutal math — ~9.4 km/s to orbit. Early guidance used gyros and analog computers; Apollo's AGC was the first digital fly-by-wire. Reentry bleeds orbital speed as heat in blunt bodies; parachutes finish the job. Tracking stations measured Doppler and ranging tones to fix orbits; ground computers (IBM 7094s at Goddard) crunched the numbers.

Applied to the Mercury Capsule (1959–1963, McDonnell): The Mercury is the 1-man's capsule.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Anatomy of Mercury Capsule — Components
body:
Every Mercury Capsule is an assembly of the early space history family's standard parts:

• Rocket stages — Stacked boosters; staging the equation.
• Engines — F-1, J-2, RL-10; turbopump-fed combustion.
• Guidance — Gyros, accelerometers, then the AGC.
• Capsule — Blunt-body reentry; Mercury/Gemini/Apollo.
• Heat shield — Ablative honeycomb taking the fire.
• Parachutes — Drogue, pilot, main — the last 10,000 feet.
• Tracking stations — MSFN dishes around the world.
• Ground computers — IBM 7094s computing orbits in real time.
• Satellite bus — Power, comms, attitude for Telstar etc.
• Spacesuit — Pressure garment; Apollo's A7L.

When examining a surviving Mercury Capsule, identify these parts in order: Rocket stages, Engines, Guidance, Capsule, Heat shield, Parachutes.

title: Early Space History Glossary
body:
The working vocabulary of early space history:

• delta-v — Velocity change; the mission's currency (km/s).
• staging — Dropping empty tanks to beat the rocket equation.
• Tsiolkovsky equation — dv = ve * ln(m0/mf); the tyranny quantified.
• rendezvous — Gemini's orbital meeting; Apollo's lunar method.
• reentry corridor — Too steep burns, too shallow skips.
• ground track — The orbit's path over Earth.
• MSFN — Manned Space Flight Network; the tracking chain.
• rope memory — Apollo's hand-woven core-rope programs.
• SPS / LM — Service propulsion and lunar module.
• space race — 1957–69 US–USSR competition.

title: Mercury Capsule in Culture
body:
'One small step' is the century's most quoted sentence. The AGC's rope memory — woven by textile workers — is engineering poetry. Mission Control's vests and consoles are period drama now. Sputnik's beep terrified and inspired; the Earthrise photo reframed humanity. 'Failure is not an option' outlived the missions.

The Mercury Capsule carries that cultural charge directly: The Mercury is the 1-man's capsule.

title: Collecting and Preserving Mercury Capsule
body:
Flown artifacts are blue-chip (provenance critical). Mission patches, photos, and documents are accessible. AGC DSKY replicas satisfy the hands-on urge. Model rockets (Estes) are the living hobby. Beware 'flown' claims without paperwork.

For the Mercury Capsule specifically: 1959's 1-man: the 1959 — the 1963's.. Prioritize completeness and originality over shine; a working Mercury Capsule with honest wear outranks a polished non-runner.

title: Mercury Capsule Restoration Guide
body:
Preserve, don't polish — space artifacts' value is in original condition. Electronics: document, don't power blindly. Paper: archival storage. Support the museums doing the real conservation.

Restoration order for a Mercury Capsule: 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical space history record without a current-limited bring-up.

title: Mercury Capsule — Rocket equation + Hohmann transfer (Runnable Python)
body:
Computes delta-v from the Tsiolkovsky equation and a Hohmann transfer to the Moon — the mission-planning math of 1969.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Mercury Capsule so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Tsiolkovsky + Hohmann transfer (public-domain astrodynamics)
import math

def rocket_dv(isp_s, mass_ratio):
    return isp_s * 9.80665 * math.log(mass_ratio) / 1000  # km/s

# Saturn V-ish: effective Isp ~300s average, mass ratio ~ 20 (3 stages compounded)
print(f"Saturn V stack dv: ~{rocket_dv(300, 20):.1f} km/s (need ~9.4 to LEO + losses)")

def hohmann(r1_km, r2_km, mu=398600.0):
    a = (r1_km + r2_km) / 2
    v1 = math.sqrt(mu / r1_km)
    vt1 = math.sqrt(mu * (2/r1_km - 1/a))
    vt2 = math.sqrt(mu * (2/r2_km - 1/a))
    v2 = math.sqrt(mu / r2_km)
    tof_days = math.pi * math.sqrt(a**3 / mu) / 86400
    return abs(vt1 - v1), abs(v2 - vt2), tof_days

dv1, dv2, days = hohmann(6578, 384400)
print(f"LEO->Moon Hohmann: burn1 {dv1:.2f} km/s, arrival {dv2:.2f} km/s, "
      f"transit {days:.1f} days")
